title: Section 85 — Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty

content.overview: BNS s. 85 — Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty (old 498A). The offence is here; the definition of cruelty is s. 86. Still cognizable and non-bailable in the usual classification.
In student language: BNS s. 85 is the rule on “Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty”. The section provides that whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 85 exists so that “Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
85. Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine

Punishment / legal consequence
Up to 3 years + fine.

learningObjectives: Master the substantive offence of matrimonial cruelty under BNS s. 85.
Identify the class of perpetrators: husband or relatives of the husband.
Understand the relationship between the penal charge under s. 85 and the statutory definition of cruelty under s. 86.
Analyze the punishment structure: imprisonment up to three years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 85 provides that whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes domestic and matrimonial abuse by holding husbands and their relatives strictly accountable for subjecting a married woman to physical or mental cruelty.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 85 (corresponding to the operative penal part of IPC s. 498A).
Perpetrators: Limited strictly to the husband or relatives of the husband.
Core offence: Subjecting the married woman to 'cruelty' (as defined in s. 86).
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to three years, and fine.
Cognate provision: Section 86 provides the comprehensive statutory definition of 'cruelty'.
essentialIngredients: The accused is either the husband or a relative of the husband of the woman.
The accused subjected the woman to cruelty as defined under Section 86.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 85 creates a dedicated criminal offence protecting women from cruelty within the matrimonial home. Under BNS 2023, the legislature bifurcated old IPC 498A into two distinct provisions: Section 85 contains the charging and penal mandate, while Section 86 provides the comprehensive substantive definition of cruelty. Liability under s. 85 is strictly confined to two categories of persons: the husband and relatives of the husband (blood relatives, relatives by marriage, or adoption). Third parties, such as distant acquaintances or paramours, cannot be charged under s. 85. The punishment extends up to three years imprisonment along with a mandatory liability for fine.
examples: Teaching example (Matrimonial harassment): A husband and his parents repeatedly lock a woman in a room without food and subject her to constant verbal abuse to force her father to transfer a residential plot to them. Both the husband and parents are liable under s. 85.

Teaching example (Non-relative excluded): A neighbor insults a married woman regarding her family's social status. The neighbor cannot be charged under s. 85 because they are not the husband or a relative of the husband.
distinctions: Section 85 vs Section 80 (Dowry death): Section 85 applies during life without requiring death; Section 80 is triggered only upon unnatural death within seven years of marriage.
Section 85 vs General Hurt (s. 115): Hurt applies to any perpetrator; Section 85 specifically penalizes cruelty committed by a husband or his relatives.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the sister-in-law of a woman residing in the same household who continuously subjected her to mental torture for failing to meet dowry demands is liable under s. 85.
Rule: A sister-in-law is a 'relative of the husband' and subjecting the woman to cruelty as defined in s. 86 establishes an offence under BNS s. 85.
Application: The relationship is established by marriage/blood and specific acts of harassment are proven.
Conclusion: The sister-in-law is liable under BNS s. 85.

Separated from the definition of cruelty which is now under s. 86.
Applies strictly to married women and matrimonial relations.
Carries imprisonment up to three years and fine.
